runs.text: The Sylhet People live in the northeast of Bangladesh between the Sylhet Division of Bangladesh and the Karimganj district of Assam, India. Sylheti in Assam’s Barak Valley face economic hardship due to geographic isolation, while northeast Bangladesh is more prosperous with tea gardens, forests, and rice farming.

Silôţ is a growing metropolitan city with a strong economy. Many Sylheti families living abroad—in the UK, the US, and the Middle East—have invested in the city to support their community. Silôţ has been a commercial center since the era of the Rajas in the ancient Brahmin kingdom.

Since the 14th century, Sufi saints (Pirs) have strongly influenced the Sylheti people. They are respected as spiritual leaders even after death, and people visit their shrines and celebrate annual festivals (urs). Many Sylhetis also practice shrine visits, believe in sorcery and the evil eye, and often seek help from religious healers instead of doctors.

Sylheti marriages usually mix Islamic and Hindu traditions and are arranged within the Sylheti-speaking community. Family ties, community involvement, and cultural preservation are highly valued. Women often face social challenges due to patriarchal norms and living with the husband’s family. Their status varies by class, and marriage can be a stressful transition for many Sylheti women.
The Sylheti language, with its own script, is spoken by about 13 million people worldwide. It gives them a
and a connection to the global Sylheti community.
The Sylheti live in a region that is internationally important for migrating birds, which may offer opportunities for Christian ornithologists or scientists to engage with the local people.

Pray for peoples with strong regional identities, reminding them that their
true citizenship is in God’s eternal Kingdom
. Pray that they may eagerly await Jesus Christ and open their hearts to God’s love beyond all borders.
May they come to share the true family bonds of God’s children as they call on the name of the Lord and believe in Jesus Christ.
Pray that Sylhetis visiting shrines will encounter Jesus, who alone can bind the powers controlling those places and release people from those demons.
Pray that the Sylheti diaspora would hear the good news and bring it back to their nation and share the Good News of Jesus with their family and neighbors.
